title: Nsight interference sweep: mixed-kernel contention and launch-pacing notes
body:
Purpose and context:
This is a working writeup of a focused Nsight Systems sweep to reproduce and characterize intermittent latency spikes we've seen in nightly perf tests for the A100 pod (dedicated pool). Prior docs focused on static occupancy numbers; this one tries to capture cross-kernel interference, CUDA graph replay jitter, and HBM/PCIe transfer coupling that shows up only under mixed workload conditions.

Cluster / HW / SW snapshot:
- Node image: rinf-a100-sxm4-2026-09
- GPU: NVIDIA A100-SXM4 40GB (driver 535.86, CUDA 12.1)
- Runtime binary: serving-runtime v1.18.3 (opt build, debug logs enabled)
- Model tested: rwd-7b-qlora (tokenization: 1-512 distribution, typical seq=128)
- Request pattern: bursty microbatching mix: 20% long (seq=512), 50% medium (seq=128), 30% short (seq=16)

Experiment goals:
1) Determine whether short kernels from concurrent control/IO tasks are descheduling/rescheduling hot SM warps on the inference kernels, reducing per-SM throughput.
2) Measure variance introduced by CUDA graph capture/replay when small host-side tasks interleave with graph replay windows.
3) Correlate HBM bandwidth stalls and L2 cache-miss bursts with observed token-latency outliers.

Instrumentation and commands used:
- Nsight Systems (CLI) capture (3 runs per config, 120s capture, sampling + CUPTI callbacks):
  nsys profile --output {out} --capture-range c --sample=cpu --system-trace on --trace=cuda,cudnn,osrt --capture-start 1 --capture-duration 120 --target-processes all --force-overwrite --stats true --env NVTX_PROFILE=1 ./run_loadgen.sh
- Nsight Compute for kernel-level breakdown (selected hot kernels):
  ncu --target-processes=all --set full --metrics sm__warps_active.avg.pct,smp__sass_thread_inst_executed.sum --kernel-name-base demoted --csv -o ncu.out ./run_kern.sh
- Extra counters via CUPTI: GPU__time_tp, sm__active_warps.avg, sm__efficiency.active_cycles_per_inst, l2__throughput.avg
- Instrumented runtime flags: --cuda-graph-replay=on|off, --launch-pacing=adaptive|fixed-2ms, --microbatch-target=8|12

Observations (short summary):
- Two classes of latency outliers: (A) reproducible 1.2–2.5x tail cases tied to CUDA graph replay windows when a host IO/kernel spike occurs; (B) rare 3x+ stalls correlated with sharp L2 miss-rate bursts and HBM write stalls.
- Nsight timeline shows that small auxiliary kernels (tensor copy + profiler heartbeats from monitoring threads) launch on overlapping SMs during graph replay and generate short (~30–150 us) kernels that preempt inference warps on SMs. Preemption is not full-context switch but leads to serialization on active warp slots resulting in reduced sustained warp occupancy.
- When CUDA graph replay is disabled, the number of (A)-type outliers drops by ~75%, but average token latency increases by ~5% due to missing replay optimizations.
- Launch-pacing adaptive mode reduced tail for mixed workload by ~40% vs fixed pacing. Pacing helps cluster short kernel launches into a less harmful cadence.

Representative trace excerpt (translated):
- t=12.331s: host schedules graph replay (kernel "graphrun_0") across 40 CUs; concurrently monitoring thread issues small memcpy_async (kernel "cpy_heart_1") -> timeline shows "cpy_heart_1" launching into same SM group 18ms after graph start; inference kernel stall observed from t=12.349s to t=12.380s (30us additional latency per token).

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Kernel launch serialization + CTA scheduling heuristics under high microbursting cause temporary underutilization of warps; small short-lived kernels get scheduled on hottest SMs and evict larger CTAs' warps from active slots.
2) CUDA graph capture/replay introduces a scheduling pattern that increases susceptibility to short-kernel interference (replay tries to maximize concurrency but is brittle to asynchronous microkernels).
3) HBM-side contention arises when multiple kernels perform small scattered writes (monitoring + checkpointing) that coincide with KV cache flushes from the runtime, causing L2 bank contention and stalls.

Quantitative notes:
- Measured sm__warps_active.avg.pct drops from ~78% steady to ~41% during interference windows for affected SMs.
- L2 miss rate spikes from 6% baseline to 29% during (B)-type events.
- Tail token latency 99.9th reduces from 480ms -> 320ms when turning off graph replay (but p50 worsens slightly).

Mitigations tried (and impact):
- Disable CUDA graph replay: + reduces tail outliers (A) substantially; - increases average latency and CPU overhead.
- Increase microbatch target from 8 -> 12: + reduces frequency of short-kernel interplay (fewer small scheduling boundaries); - slightly increases memory pressure and inc GPU memory fragmentation.
- Adaptive launch-pacing: + best overall improvement (reduces harmful overlap); implemented a simple token-bucket pacing in runtime and saw ~40% reduction in tail events in the sweep.
- Move monitoring IO to a separate GPU stream with explicit stream priority and stream wait semantics; + reduces direct kernel overlap but introduces host-side coupling; partial improvement.

Open experiments to run (next steps):
- Re-run sweep on H100 to check whether newer scheduling/hardware mitigates preemption behavior (driver differences might change CTA eviction semantics).
- Add synthetic microkernel generator to vary kernel duration from 10us -> 500us to map eviction thresholds and determine safe pacing windows.
- Try tuned stream priority + GPU-side semaphore (cuSignal/Wait) to serialize monitoring kernels outside replay windows.
- Instrument runtime to coalesce monitoring writes into larger batched copies to reduce HBM small-write pressure.

Action items:
- Evan: implement adaptive token-bucket launch-pacing prototype in v1.18.4 branch (PR linked). Target: reduce tail for mixed-workload nightlies. (ETA 2026-11-12)
- Priya: synthetic microkernel harness + param grid for duration/amplitude. Run on dedicated testbed. (ETA 2026-11-09)
- Liam: test same sweep on H100 preprod node, capture Nsight baseline. (ETA 2026-11-10)

Notes & random observations (scratchpad):
- CUDA graph replay sometimes collapses multiple dependent small memcpy kernels into a single replayed kernel which changes the launch frontier and makes interference non-linear.
- Host CPU context-switches (ksoftirqd bursts) coincide with a fraction of outliers; OS noise mitigation might help.
- We should add a small NVTX marker when monitoring threads issue GPU work so traces can be filtered quickly.

References and links:
- Linked PR (prototype pacing): https://git.redwood/repo/serving-runtime/pull/982
- Jira ticket tracking: RED-4321
- Quick look confluence notes: confluence:serving/runtime/profiles/interference-sweep-2026

Status: draft — want to run the H100 sweep before making recommendations final.
